I had the chance to check out Goldman Sachs' "AI Is Becoming a Stock Picker's Market" and I agree with most of what's being shared.

The AI trade stopped being one trade, and that's the most bullish thing that could happen to it.

Since 2023-2024 you could buy anything with AI in the deck and it went up with everything else.

This summer was different. Half of the ten biggest tech names were up and the other half were down, and Nasdaq multiples have compressed about 20% this year with the 10-year above 5.25%.

That is what a maturing cycle looks like. 

When multiples stop expanding, earnings have to do the work, and earnings are where this trade is strongest this Q. 
$MU
 just guided to $61.5B for a single quarter, lead times across the supply chain are still stretching, and semis trade at a discount to the S&P.

A market that moves together rewards being early, and we've had plenty of that over the last year.But that phase is mostly gone. 

A market that splits apart rewards knowing where the bottleneck is, layer by layer, and which companies get paid when it tightens. 

Not all companies are created equal, and we are seeing big dispersion between them.

A year ago the easy money was just owning the right theme. Now it goes to the right companies within each theme, and to knowing what sets them apart.
